## Three Birds, Endless Stuffings: Your Thanksgiving 2026 Guide


Gourmet Butcher Block The All-Madden Turducken


The turducken (a deboned chicken inside a deboned duck inside a deboned turkey) comes from South Louisiana’s Cajun country. There, the biggest variation is the stuffing: cornbread dressing, andouille sausage, dirty rice, shrimp, crawfish, and more. Louisiana makers also sell related dishes like the turporken, which swaps the duck for pork, and the deboned stuffed turkey. Outside the U.S., the closest relatives are Britain’s three-bird roast and France’s legendary *rôti sans pareil* .


**Turducken variations at a glance**


- **Classic Cajun turducken:** turkey, duck, and chicken with Cajun cornbread or pork cornbread stuffing
- **Sausage-stuffed turducken:** layered with andouille or pork sausage stuffing, like the All-Madden Turducken
- **Seafood-stuffed turducken:** layered with shrimp or crawfish étouffée stuffing
- **Rice-stuffed turducken:** layered with dirty rice, wild rice and pecan, or broccoli cheese and rice
- **Turporken:** a deboned turkey stuffed with boneless pork and chicken
- **Deboned stuffed turkey:** a single boneless turkey filled with Cajun stuffing
- **Turduckhen and gooducken:** a Cornish game hen in place of the chicken, or goose in place of the turkey
- **Three-bird roast:** Britain’s version of a layered, deboned bird roast

## **Where did the turducken come from?**


The turducken was born in South Louisiana, but who made the first one is disputed. Hebert’s Specialty Meats, a Cajun butcher shop opened in Maurice, Louisiana, in 1984 by brothers Junior and Sammy Hebert, says it created the turducken after a customer’s request. Chef Paul Prudhomme also popularized the dish and trademarked the name “Turducken” in 1986.


The turducken went national on December 1, 1996. Glenn Mistich of Gourmet Butcher Block in Gretna, Louisiana, brought one to broadcaster John Madden before a Saints game against the St. Louis Rams. Madden ate it on air and made it a fixture of his Thanksgiving broadcasts.

## **Where is turducken most popular?**


Turducken is still most closely tied to Louisiana and the Gulf South, where Cajun butchers and specialty meat shops make and sell them by the thousands each holiday season. Since Madden made it famous in the 1990s, Louisiana makers have shipped turduckens nationwide. Today it shows up on Thanksgiving tables across the country, especially among football fans and anyone who loves Cajun food.


## **Regional Variations**


You could have a turducken the standard way, but why not ask yourself how turducken is made regionally — and then try one of these specialities!


- **Cajun turducken** : Get a little spicy with a **[cajun turducken](https://www.goldbelly.com/collections/cajun-turkey)** , stuffed with one (or all) of traditional cajun foods: andouille, rice, and crawfish.
- **Creole turducken:** Dive into the NOLA vibes with a Creole turducken — it’s stuffed with cornbread dressing and oysters.
- **Southern BBQ twist:** Bring some BBQ to your birds with a good, old-fashioned smoker. This southern twist pops the whole bird-bake into the smoker to add another layer of flavor.
- **Gourmet urban variations:** Fly through the gourmet circuit with things like truffle stuffing inside the chicken or surrounding the layers. Don’t forget to stop by a specialty shop to get your turducken made with artisanal meats.
- **Holiday mash-ups:** Not a fan of all three birds in the turducken? Mix it up a bit with a porkducken (chicken stuffed in a duck stuffed in a pig) or leave the triple-food plan for dessert with a **[piecaken](https://blog.goldbelly.com/what-is-piecaken/)** — three or more pies layered inside a cake.

## **FAQs**


**Where did turducken originate?**


In South Louisiana’s Cajun country. Hebert’s Specialty Meats in Maurice, Louisiana, says it created the turducken, and Chef Paul Prudhomme trademarked the name in 1986.


**Is turducken only Southern?**


Turducken started in Louisiana and is still most closely tied to Cajun cooking, but Louisiana makers now ship turduckens nationwide.


**Can you order turducken online?**


You can order your own turducken online at[Goldbelly.com](http://goldbelly.com/) , in both small and large sizes.


**What is a turporken?**


A turporken is a deboned turkey stuffed with boneless pork and chicken, with layers of stuffing in between. It’s a Louisiana variation on the turducken.
